map.每寸折量 = 实测长度(cm) ÷ 标准寸数；取穴距离 = 目标寸数 × 每寸折: cm per cun = measured length (cm) ÷ standard cun count; location distance = target cun × cm per cun; reverse cun = measured distance (cm) ÷ cm per cun
map.先用该段体表的实测长度除以教材规定的标准寸数，得到此患者「1 寸折合多少厘米」；: First divide the measured length of the body-surface segment by the standard cun count in the textbook to obtain how many centimeters one cun equals for this patient. Then multiply the target cun count by the cm-per-cun value to get the measuring distance from the starting point along the segment. Conversely, after measuring a distance in centimeters on the body surface, divide it by the cm-per-cun value to get the corresponding cun count, which can be used to check whether the point already located has deviated. Note: the cun count is proportioned to this segment itself, so the cm-per-cun value differs between segments of the same patient and applying one segment's value to another introduces error. The result is for study and point-location reference only; actual location must still combine bony landmarks and a physician's judgment.

Reverse check: if a point measures 5 cm from the wrist crease, then 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5 cun, which helps judge whether that point is near the intended 2 cun.
map.反算寸数有什么用？: What is the reverse cun calculation used for?

The cm-per-cun value differs between segments, so the reverse calculation must use the measured length of that segment itself.
